data.title: Luca Mining Provides Clarification Regarding Media-Reported Statements Related to the Campo Morado Mine
data.description:
Luca Mining Provides Clarification Regarding Media-Reported Statements Related to the Campo Morado Mine

Luca Mining Provides Clarification Regarding Media-Reported Statements Related to the Campo Morado Mine

PR Newswire

VANCOUVER, BC, Nov. 22, 2026

VANCOUVER, BC, Nov. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Luca Mining Corp. ("Luca" or the "Company") (TSXV: LUCA) (OTCQX: LUCMF) (Frankfurt: Z68) wishes to clarify recent reports published by various Mexican media outlets stating that the Company's Campo Morado Mine, located in Arcelia, Guerrero State, Mexico, is controlled by a criminal organization.

These reports are categorically false. The Campo Morado Mine is owned and operated by Luca through its wholly owned subsidiary, Minas de Campo Morado, S.A. de C.V., and Luca has sole operational and financial control of the mine. Neither Luca nor any of its directors, officers or employees has any affiliation with the individuals mentioned in those reports.

Luca is not aware of any active or, to its knowledge, pending investigation by any authority in connection with these matters at its Campo Morado Mine. The Company believes the source of the reports may have confused Luca's business and affairs with other mining operations near the town of Campo Morado, which is unconnected with the Campo Morado mine, and with which Luca has no operational history.

Minas de Campo Morado, S.A. de C.V. operates under valid federal mining concessions and environmental permits, is subject to oversight by Mexican authorities, including the Army Ministry for the use of explosives in the mine, sells its concentrates to an established international buyer, and continues to operate in the normal course. Luca has formally requested that the outlets reporting on the Campo Morado mine correct their reports. Luca reiterates its commitment to transparency and will cooperate with the authorities if requested.

About Luca Mining Corp.

Luca Mining Corp. (TSX-V: LUCA, OTCQX: LUCMF, Frankfurt: Z68) is a Canadian mining company with two wholly owned mines located in the prolific Sierra Madre mineralized belt in Mexico. These mines produce gold, silver, zinc, copper, and lead and generate strong cash flow. Both mines have considerable development and resource upside as well as district-scale exploration potential. The Company has also entered into definitive agreements to acquire the Cozamin Mine, an underground copper-silver operation in Zacatecas State, and the El Barqueño project in Jalisco State, each subject to customary closing conditions.

The Company's Campo Morado Mine hosts VMS-style, polymetallic mineralization within a large land package comprising 121 square kilometres. It is an underground operation, producing zinc, copper, gold, silver and lead. The mine is located in Guerrero State.

The Tahuehueto Mine is a large property of over 100 square kilometres in Durango State. The project hosts epithermal gold and silver vein-style mineralization. Tahuehueto is a newly constructed underground mining operation producing primarily gold and silver. The Company has successfully commissioned its mill and is now in commercial production.

On Behalf of the Board of Directors
(signed) "Dan Barnholden"

Dan Barnholden, Chief Executive Officer

For more information, please visit: www.lucamining.com

data.title: TTW Reveals Top 50 Best Countries in the World to Travel in 2027
data.description:
TTW Reveals Top 50 Best Countries in the World to Travel in 2027

TTW Reveals Top 50 Best Countries in the World to Travel in 2027

PR Newswire

NEW YORK, Nov. 22, 2026

NEW YORK, Nov. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- TTW has released its editorial selection of the top 50 best countries to travel in the world in 2027, placing Australia first and highlighting ten leading entries in this announcement. The United Kingdom, France, the United States, Brazil, Portugal, Austria, Indonesia, Hungary and India complete the list of best countries around the world to travel for next year. The selection brings together cultural cities, coastal destinations and opportunities for outdoor exploration, giving travellers a starting point for planning journeys around their interests and travel preferences.

The United States ranks 18th in the global selection, recognised for its iconic attractions, national parks, entertainment destinations and cultural diversity. New York City's landmarks, the Grand Canyon and New Orleans' historic French Quarter remain major tourism draws. The country will also host Super Bowl LXI at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California, on 14 February 2027, creating an additional attraction for international sports travellers. Meanwhile, countries across Europe, Asia, Africa, Oceania and Latin America feature prominently, reflecting the diversity of experiences available worldwide.

The ranking presents countries through the destinations that help explain their appeal. Sydney anchors Australia's entry, while Edinburgh and London represent contrasting British city experiences. Elsewhere, the selection connects island settings with historic centres, museums with neighbourhood life, and familiar landmarks with places that reward a longer stay. The complete guide includes country rankings, continents and featured destinations, supported by detailed profiles that help readers compare different styles of holiday before deciding where to travel.

"As international tourism enters an era of unprecedented transformation, destinations must distinguish themselves not merely through grandeur, but through authenticity, sustainability and cultural sophistication. Our 2027 ranking reflects this evolving philosophy, recognising countries that offer compelling experiences while preserving their distinctive identities.

The future of travel belongs to destinations capable of harmonising economic prosperity with environmental responsibility and meaningful cultural exchange. At Travel And Tour World, our endeavour is to celebrate this remarkable global tapestry and inspire travellers to venture beyond familiar horizons, discovering the extraordinary possibilities that await across continents," added Anup Kumar Keshan, Founder and Editor-in-Chief, Travel And Tour World (TTW).

The World's Top Five Best Countries to Travel in 2027

Australia takes first place, offering an extraordinary combination of coastal landscapes, wildlife experiences and cultural attractions. Sydney's Opera House, the Great Barrier Reef, Uluru and Tasmania remain among its most celebrated destinations. The Men's Rugby World Cup, scheduled from 1 October to 13 November 2027 across seven host cities, provides another reason to visit. Travellers can combine sporting events with reef excursions, Aboriginal cultural experiences and regional nature adventures.

Switzerland ranks second, celebrated for its Alpine scenery, scenic rail journeys and picturesque lakeside towns. The Matterhorn, Jungfrau region, Lucerne and Lake Geneva attract visitors throughout the year. The FIS Alpine World Ski Championships, scheduled in Crans-Montana from 1 to 14 February 2027, add further appeal for winter sports enthusiasts. Switzerland's mountain resorts, historic architecture and panoramic transport networks support diverse travel experiences.

Japan secures third place, combining contemporary urban culture with centuries-old traditions. Tokyo, Kyoto and Hokkaido provide contrasting experiences through modern attractions, historic temples, regional cuisine and natural landscapes. Yokohama's International Horticultural Expo, scheduled from 19 March to 26 September 2027, introduces another major tourism attraction, particularly for visitors interested in gardens, horticulture and cultural exhibitions.

Canada occupies fourth position, offering expansive wilderness, multicultural cities and Indigenous cultural heritage. The Canadian Rockies, Vancouver's waterfront, Québec City's historic neighbourhoods and Stanley Park provide diverse sightseeing opportunities. Visitors can explore mountain scenery, participate in guided Indigenous cultural experiences and discover the country's distinctive regional traditions.

Thailand completes the top five, attracting international travellers with Buddhist heritage, tropical beaches and renowned culinary experiences. Bangkok's Grand Palace, Ayutthaya's historic temples, Chiang Mai's cultural landmarks and Krabi's coastal scenery remain major attractions. The Udon Thani International Horticultural Expo, continuing until 14 March 2027, creates additional opportunities to explore northeastern Thailand.

TTW global travel ranking places Fiji at 40th, followed by Panama, Indonesia, Belize, Ecuador, Egypt, Russia, Kenya, South Africa, Colombia and Tanzania. These countries offer diverse tourism experiences, including tropical islands, wildlife safaris, cultural heritage, ancient landmarks and natural wonders, appealing to travellers seeking memorable international journeys.

Egypt occupies 45th position, with the total solar eclipse on 2 August 2027 expected to provide a distinctive astronomical tourism opportunity around Luxor. The Pyramids of Giza, Grand Egyptian Museum and Nile Valley heritage sites remain prominent attractions.

Russia completes the ranking in 46th position, featuring Moscow, Saint Petersburg, Lake Baikal and the Altai Mountains. However, significant security concerns and official travel warnings, including UK advice against all travel, remain important considerations.

Kenya follows in 47th position, offering wildlife safaris across the Maasai Mara and Amboseli National Park. Its role as another Africa Cup of Nations co-host provides opportunities to combine football tourism with nature exploration.

South Africa, ranked 48th, will co-host the ICC Men's Cricket World Cup from 2 October to 21 November 2027. Cape Town, Table Mountain, the Garden Route and Kruger National Park offer additional tourism experiences.

Colombia occupies 49th place, recognised for Cartagena's colonial heritage, Tayrona National Natural Park, the Coffee Cultural Landscape and the mountain scenery surrounding Salento and the Cocora Valley.

Tanzania, ranked 50th, combines the Serengeti, Ngorongoro, Mount Kilimanjaro and Zanzibar with international sports tourism. The country will co-host the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations from 19 June to 17 July.

To explore full rankings, click on the report "TTW Releases 50 Best Countries to Travel in 2027".

Global Tourism Opportunities in 2027
The ranking highlights the importance of international sporting events, cultural exhibitions, natural attractions and regional experiences in shaping travel opportunities for 2027. Australia's Rugby World Cup, Japan's horticultural exhibition, the Africa Cup of Nations and South Africa's Cricket World Cup provide notable event-driven travel opportunities.

The selection also demonstrates the appeal of wildlife tourism, tropical island holidays, archaeological exploration and cultural discovery. Travellers are encouraged to consider official travel advisories, entry requirements, transportation arrangements and confirmed event schedules before booking.

Previously, Travel And Tour World published the following articles:Top 50 Christmas Holiday Destinations Around the World for 2026 , Top 50 Thanksgiving Travel Destinations in the World for 2026 Travel And Tour World Spotlights Top 30 Halloween Travel Destinations in the Americas and Caribbean for 2026 Travel And Tour World Announces Top 50 Halloween Travel Destinations in the World for 2026 TTW Names Top 30 Shopping Travel Destinations in the Americas and Caribbean for 2026 and more. 

Methodology
TTW's 50 Best Countries to Travel in 2027 selection provides an editorial assessment of destinations based on their tourism attractions, cultural heritage, natural landscapes and significant events. The guide considers internationally recognised landmarks, wildlife destinations, outdoor activities, regional traditions and opportunities for cultural exploration.

Particular attention is given to major sporting tournaments, horticultural exhibitions, astronomical events and cultural programmes scheduled for 2027. Destination profiles also examine opportunities to explore beyond established tourism centres, connecting popular attractions with regional communities and distinctive landscapes.

Practical travel considerations, including seasonal conditions, transport arrangements, accessibility and official travel advisories, provide additional context. The selection is intended to support destination discovery and travel planning rather than serve as a statistical measure of visitor satisfaction.

About Travel And Tour World (TTW)
Travel And Tour World (TTW) is an international digital travel media platform with 15 million readers, covering global tourism, aviation, hospitality, airlines, cruises, destinations and travel industry developments. Through destination features, travel news, tourism reports and industry insights, TTW provides information for international travellers, tourism professionals and industry stakeholders. Its editorial coverage explores emerging tourism trends, destination marketing, hospitality developments, major international events and evolving travel opportunities. TTW aims to connect the global travel community through informative journalism and destination-focused reporting, helping readers discover international destinations, understand developments across the tourism industry and make informed travel decisions in an increasingly interconnected global travel market.

data.title: Medicare beneficiaries could skip the nursing home for cheaper care at home under new bill
data.description:
By Jessica Hall

The plan would free up hospital and nursing-home beds - and lower costs

Care at home could help cut costs, make patients more comfortable and free up much-needed hospital and nursing-home beds, proponents of the bill said.

A new bipartisan bill would create a five-year pilot program for Medicare beneficiaries to receive nursing care and intensive rehabilitation services in their home rather than in a nursing facility.

After a hospital stay, Medicare beneficiaries who need additional care often get transferred on a short-term basis to nursing homes for rehabilitation. The new proposal would allow those patients to get a higher level of nursing care at home, with the goal of freeing up hospital and nursing-home beds, lowering costs and keeping patients more comfortable in their own homes. The bill, called the Bringing Rehabilitation, Integrated Delivery, and Greater Extended Care at Home Act, was introduced by Rep. Adrian Smith, a Nebraska Republican, and Rep. Debbie Dingell, a Democrat from Michigan.

"When it comes to healthcare, one size does not fit all, and patients deserve to have choices. Too often, options are unnecessarily restricted - especially for Medicare beneficiaries," Smith said in a press statement.

The bill also calls for a study to be conducted comparing the quality, outcomes and costs of home care versus facility-based care.

"Most patients prefer to receive care at home, so we must do more to support access to skilled nursing care in the home for patients who prefer that option. And most importantly, it is the less expensive option for both families and the government," Dingell said in a press statement.

The proposal comes as Americans are living longer but not always remaining in good health. There's a difference of about 12 years between a person's lifespan and their so-called healthspan - the number of years they are healthy - according to research from Age Wave, a think tank and consultancy focused on aging and longevity.

If people are living longer with disease and disability, obtaining care and finding caregivers will become more of an issue. As many as 77% of people ages 50 and older want to remain in their own home as they age, according to AARP. Nursing homes, meanwhile, are facing financial pressures and staffing shortages, with hundreds having closed since the COVID-19 pandemic, especially in rural areas. A JAMA Internal Medicine study found that national nursing home capacity dropped 5% from 2019 to 2024.

"Seniors deserve to be able to receive timely, safe, and high-quality care after a hospital stay. Whether this can be achieved in the home on a national scale is something that requires thoughtful consideration - especially given that our nation is aging and caregiver shortages are growing across health care," Dan Ciolek, associate vice president of therapy advocacy for the American Health Care Association/National Center for Assisted Living, the industry trade group for nursing homes and assisted-living facilities, said in an email to MarketWatch. "We look forward to working with Congress on viable, innovative solutions to ensure that seniors get the care they need in the setting best suited to them."

The proposal follows another Medicare pilot program called Acute Hospital Care at Home that received a five-year extension earlier this year. Under that program, Medicare beneficiaries can get hospital-level care for conditions such as acute infection, heart failure or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease in their own home.

"Hospital at home demonstrated that seniors can be treated at home safely and effectively. The BRIDGE Care at Home Act would test the idea of skilled nursing and intensive rehabilitation services at home, helping patients maintain their independence, supporting caregivers and giving providers an alternative to working in an institutional setting," Krista Drobac, the founder of Moving Health Home, a coalition of healthcare organizations that advocates for home-based care, said in a press statement.

Getting skilled-nursing rehabilitation in the home would allow "patients to rebuild functional independence directly in the spaces where they actually live. Patients sleep better, move more and face lower risks of delirium and ... complications when their acute recovery happens at home," Swetha Gudibanda, medical director of Sanford Health Marshfield Clinic Home Recovery Care in Marshfield, Wis., said in statement in support of the BRIDGE proposal.

-Jessica Hall

How to Short Anthropic (ANT): Leverage Shares by Themes Explains ANDD and ANSS Inverse Anthropic ETFs, Short Selling and Put Options

GREENWICH, Conn., Nov. 22, 2026

With Anthropic now trading on Nasdaq (ticker: ANT), Leverage Shares by Themes outlines three ways investors can take a bearish view on Anthropic stock, including planned 2X Short (ANDD) and 1X Short (ANSS) Anthropic ETFs.

GREENWICH, Conn., Nov. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Leverage Shares by Themes today published a guide for investors exploring how to short Anthropic stock following the company's highly anticipated initial public offering. Anthropic, PBC priced its IPO at $83.00 per share on November 18, 2026, raising approximately $81.3 billion through the offering of 980 million Class A shares. The stock began trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker ANT on November 19, opening at $111.50 per share.

With Anthropic now publicly traded, investors can evaluate different approaches to gaining inverse exposure to its stock, including traditional short selling, put options and the planned Leverage Shares 2X Short Anthropic Daily ETF (ANDD) and Leverage Shares 1X Short Anthropic Daily ETF (ANSS)

How Can You Short Anthropic Stock?
Now that ANT is trading, some investors may want to express a bearish view. There are three common ways to short Anthropic stock: sell borrowed shares in a margin account, buy put options once options on ANT are listed, or buy an inverse ETF designed to move opposite to the stock on a given day.

Short Selling Anthropic Stock
Short selling means borrowing ANT shares through a brokerage, selling them and buying them back later. It needs a margin account, and newly listed stocks can be hard or expensive to borrow. Losses have no upper limit because there is no limit to how far a share price can rise, and a rising price can trigger margin calls.

Buying Put Options on ANT
A put option gives its buyer the right to sell ANT at a set price before a set date. Listed options on ANT will not be available on its first trading day: exchange rules allow options on a large new listing to begin trading no earlier than the second business day after the IPO day. The most a put buyer can lose is the premium paid, and options lose value as their expiration date approaches.

Inverse Anthropic ETFs: ANDD and ANSS
The Leverage Shares 2X Short Anthropic Daily ETF (ANDD) will seek -200% (-2X), and the Leverage Shares 1X Short Anthropic Daily ETF (ANSS) will seek -100% (-1X), of the daily performance of Anthropic common stock, before fees and expenses. Once launched, they will trade like any ETF on Cboe, with no margin account and no share borrowing needed, and an investor cannot lose more than the amount invested. An investor could lose the full amount invested in ANDD if Anthropic's stock price rises by more than 50% in a single trading day.

ANUU, ANDD and ANSS are not yet trading. Their first trading date on Cboe is November 23, 2026.

What Is the Difference Between ANDD and ANSS?
ANDD seeks twice the inverse of Anthropic's daily move; ANSS seeks the inverse without additional leverage. If ANT falls 5% in a day, ANDD seeks a 10% gain and ANSS a 5% gain for that day, before fees and expenses. If ANT rises 5% in a day, ANDD seeks a 10% loss and ANSS a 5% loss.

"Shorting a stock on the day it lists is harder than most people expect, because borrowing can be scarce and options are not there yet," said Paul Marino, Chief Revenue Officer, Themes ETFs. "ANDD and ANSS are built to give active traders a daily inverse view on Anthropic in a standard ETF wrapper, and we want them to understand exactly how the daily reset works before they use either one."

Frequently Asked Questions

Can You Short Anthropic on Its First Trading Day?
Short selling ANT on November 19 depends on whether your brokerage can locate shares to borrow. Listed options on ANT and the ANDD and ANSS ETFs will not be available that day.

Is There an Inverse ETF for Anthropic?
Leverage Shares by Themes has two: ANDD, which will seek -2X the daily performance of Anthropic stock, and ANSS, which will seek -1X. Both seek their objectives for a single day only.

Can You Lose More Than You Invest When Shorting Anthropic?
With short selling, yes, because losses grow as long as the price rises. With a put option the loss is limited to the premium paid. With ANDD or ANSS the loss is limited to the amount invested, which can be lost in full.

Specialised Therapeutics and DKSH Partner to Expand Access to Cancer Medicines in Vietnam

PR Newswire

SINGAPORE, Nov. 22, 2026

SINGAPORE, Nov. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Singapore-based independent biopharmaceutical company Specialised Therapeutics (ST) and DKSH have signed an exclusive strategic partnership to bring innovative oncology therapies to patients across Vietnam.

According to 2022 GLOBOCAN estimates from the World Health Organization, Vietnam faces a significant and growing cancer burden, with approximately 180,000 new cases and over 120,000 deaths reported annually. The collaboration will directly target two major areas of concern: breast cancer, which is the most frequently diagnosed cancer among Vietnamese women, and lung cancer, a leading cause of cancer-related mortality (GLOBOCAN 2022).

ST currently commercialises oncology products under exclusive licenses covering Southeast Asia, Australia, and New Zealand. The company has successfully secured regulatory approvals in major markets including Australia, New Zealand, Singapore, Thailand, and Malaysia. According to ST, this new partnership in Vietnam strategically extends its regional model into one of Southeast Asia's largest and fastest-growing healthcare markets.

"Vietnam is a priority market for ST, and the right partner makes all the difference," said Carlo Montagner, Chief Executive Officer of Specialised Therapeutics. "DKSH brings deep local market knowledge and expertise, and we look forward to introducing several vital cancer medicines to patients in Vietnam over the next few years."

"We are proud to partner with Specialised Therapeutics to strengthen access to specialty oncology care in Vietnam," said Charaf Kadri, Vice President, Healthcare, DKSH. "At DKSH, our commitment to 'Healthcare for All' drives everything we do. By combining ST's specialty oncology expertise with DKSH's local market knowledge and capabilities, we aim to help improve healthcare outcomes across Vietnam."

About Specialised Therapeutics

Founded in 2007 and headquartered in Singapore, Specialised Therapeutics (ST) is an independent specialty pharmaceutical company bringing breakthrough therapies and medical technologies to patients across Australia, New Zealand, and Southeast Asia. ST partners with global pharmaceutical, biotech, and diagnostic leaders to commercialise advanced healthcare solutions across a broad range of conditions. Leveraging deep expertise in complex regulatory, reimbursement, and commercial environments, the company is dedicated to addressing unmet medical needs and expanding access to essential treatments for underserved communities. Its growing portfolio, featuring more than 18 global brands, covers oncology, haematology, CNS, neurology, endocrinology, ophthalmology, and dermatology, among other therapeutic areas. Learn more at www.stbiopharma.com. 

About DKSH

For more than 160 years, DKSH has been delivering growth for companies in Asia Pacific, Europe, and North America across its Business Units Healthcare, Consumer Goods, Performance Materials, and Technology. As a leading Market Expansion Services provider, DKSH offers sourcing, market access support, market insights, marketing and sales, logistics as well as after-sales services, following its purpose of enriching people's lives. DKSH is a participant of the United Nations Global Compact and adheres to its principles-based approach to responsible business. Listed on the SIX Swiss Exchange, DKSH operates in 35 markets with 26,840 specialists, generating net sales of CHF 11.1 billion in 2025. www.dksh.com

Forward-looking statements

This release contains forward-looking statements, including on regulatory submissions, approvals and product launches in Vietnam. Actual outcomes may differ materially and depend on regulatory decisions and other factors outside the companies' control.

data.title: These little-known investments could be among the best bargains in a crash
data.description:
By Brett Arends

In these febrile markets, be prepared

As market turmoil spreads, be prepared - for opportunities

If this stock market turmoil turns into a full-blown crash, look for low-risk investment bargains among closed-end funds.

In a liquidation panic - such as during the 2008-09 financial crisis, or the COVID-19 stock-market crisis of March 2020 - these funds often fall to huge discounts to their underlying net asset value, offering what may be the closest thing you'll ever see to a free lunch.

To be sure, nobody knows if this turmoil will develop into a major crash or a bear market. So far, the selloff - although it seems steep now - should be viewed in context. It's barely six weeks since the S&P 500 was at all-time highs. Since then, it's down only about 8%. The index is still up about 5% this year.

What will happen next? Screenwriter William Goldman's famous comment about Hollywood applies equally well to Wall Street. "Nobody knows anything. Not one person in the entire motion picture field knows for a certainty what's going to work."

But it's a matter of being prepared. Those who bought stocks during past panics generally earned spectacular investment returns - so long as they bought wisely, of course.

Closed-end funds are the redheaded stepchild of the mutual-fund industry. Unlike exchange-traded funds and traditional mutual funds, they don't issue new shares when investors put money into the fund, and they don't redeem the shares when investors sell. Instead, there are a limited number of shares, and they trade on the market like a company's shares. To invest in the fund, an investor would need to get their broker to buy them off an existing investor who wants to sell. For those wanting to get out of the fund, they would need to find an investor who wants to buy.

This unique feature gives closed-end funds one special characteristic: The share price is not governed by the underlying net asset value of the fund's investments. A closed-end fund could theoretically own, say, $10 a share in no-risk Treasury bills, but the share price could still fly all over the place based on what's happening in the stock market.

In a crash, the share prices often fall off a cliff. Far more so than the underlying investments. So this can give investors a double bargain: The stocks, bonds and so on that the fund holds may have gone down with the market, making them cheaper, while the stock of the fund itself may have fallen even further.

At the depths of the March 2020 COVID panic, solid, well-run closed-end funds that invested in everything from stocks to real estate to municipal bonds saw their fund's shares fall to 20% or more below the underlying value of the investments - which were, themselves, sharply down. When the market recovered, the investments rose - and the share price rose even more.

There are hundreds of funds out there, and they range from the excellent to the dismal.

One worth a look (for example) is Source Capital SOR.

This is a conservative "balanced portfolio" fund run by FPA Advisors, a firm known for its cautious approach to markets. It successfully dodged the infamous dot-com bubble at the turn of the millennium and suffered comparatively small losses during the global financial crisis of 2008-09. Over the past 10 years, Source has outperformed its benchmark, which is a theoretical portfolio consisting of 60% global equities and 40% U.S. bonds. The fund is co-managed by Steve Romick, better known for running the $12.5 billion FPA Crescent FPACX mutual fund. (Source has just $410 million in assets.)

Source came into this selloff conservatively positioned. That included a hefty 16% of the portfolio held in cash and equivalents, such as Treasury bills. FPA partner Ryan Leggio told me the cash position is unusually high because the fund has been selling bonds this year and hasn't found enough good value investment opportunities.

He said the fund has a policy of buying back shares in the market whenever the discount to net asset value is more than 10%. After the turmoil of recent weeks, SOR at $45.50 a share on Thursday was selling at a 9% discount, equivalent to buying investments at 91 cents on the dollar.

The fees, 0.98% a year, are higher than in most low-cost index funds. But then there's the discount, the outperformance, and all that cash on the balance sheet.

None of this means a full-blown crash will happen. But it's always good to be prepared.

-Brett Arends
